# Reports say most AI agents still skip the semantic layer when they query data

A cluster of wire stories this window converges on one theme: surveys and vendor commentary suggest AI agents mostly bypass semantic layers when generating queries, and enterprises are seeing the data errors that result. Elsewhere, BI tool releases lean into governing AI-generated SQL rather than just running it, and the rest of the window is mostly beginner dbt tutorials.

## Top stories
- **[Few AI agents rely on semantic layers](https://news.google.?oc=5)** — VentureBeat, with a companion piece ([Semantic layers may not be read by AI agents](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMikgFBVV95cUxOLWNtdGdZSkdzM2ttWk9ob1NGcVdCUXcxUTJrbnoyT2FRWlVhZGFmQ2FnU1ZlQUJ2REtDREs4OVZYV2l3M29hLUJVR0pJdUpHVUptSnRmbWdvRDdqakh2TDM5cUtKWmtqMV9DZHpjcFlkZGJsRmF6RFI3ZDZIRnhjUlo0a1JKWWhtT0UxSUhLalRnUQ?oc=5) and a related finding that [64% of enterprises find AI errors in data](https://news.google.?oc=5). Coverage on the same day argues most production AI agents generate SQL directly against raw tables rather than going through a governed semantic layer, and ties that to a majority of enterprises reporting AI-introduced data errors. *Why it matters:* the semantic layer's whole pitch is a single governed definition of a metric; if agents route around it, teams are back to reconciling inconsistent numbers, just with an LLM doing the querying instead of an analyst.

## Releases & tools
- **[Lightdash 2.481.0](https://github.com/lightdash/lightdash/releases/tag/2.481.0)** — the latest of three releases this window adds Claude Haiku 5.5 presets, per-app LLM gateway URLs, and tracking of AI agent SQL approval decisions, continuing Lightdash's push into governing AI-generated queries rather than just serving dashboards.
- **[Cube v1.8.2](https://github.com/cube-js/cube/releases/tag/v1.8.2)** — rolls up three releases with fixes to join-hint enrichment on cyclic join trees, masking of pre-aggregated members, and rolling-window date-range handling, plus faster UNION ALL planning over rollup partitions.
- **[Great Expectations 1.24.0](https://github.com/fivetran/great_expectations/releases/tag/1.24.0)** — adds Python 3.14 support, with the clickhouse and teradata extras not yet supported on that version.

## Worth reading
- **[The SQL Looked Right. The Number Wasn't.](https://medium.com/@seanlukeholland/the-sql-looked-right-the-number-wasnt-06f92cbd6ec2)** — Medium. Four modelling decisions from building a SaaS retention model in dbt, written with an eye to AI increasingly writing the queries on top of that model.
